To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
teachers' perceptions of ERB vary according to gender, rural-urban location, and job satisfaction and personal teaching efficacy.

female teachers are more willing to volunteer in extra roles towards co-workers than male teachers; that rural teachers are less enthusiastic about extra roles towards students and the organisation than their urban and suburban colleagues; that personal teaching efficacy and teacher job satisfaction are important predictors of teachers' extra-role behaviour; and that the socio-demographic variables have a marginal contribution in predicting teachers' extra roles.

(1) teachers in rural schools are less willing to volunteer for ERB than those in urban and suburban areas; (2) females are more willing to volunteer than males; (3) teachers' personal characteristics (i e. job satisfaction and teaching efficacy) are significant predictors of ERB.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of ERB in school effectiveness.
how teachers' perceptions of their own extra-role behaviours are related to school effectiveness in Southern Ethiopia.
the role of extra-roles as a factor in the effective functioning of educational organisations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the findings of this study have significant implications for school effectiveness.
the findings of this study are consistent with the findings of previous research in that the teachers' willingness to perform ERB is positively related to their job-related personal characteristics.
teachers' willingness to engage in extra-roles is a significant factor for the success and effectiveness of school.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
teachers who are satisfied with their jobs and who have high personal teaching efficacy are more likely to engage themselves in ERB.
the ERB of school teachers is an important factor in determining the effectiveness of schools.
ERB has significant implications on school effectiveness.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ERB of teachers is not a random phenomenon.
the ERB of teachers is a complex phenomenon that needs to be understood and addressed from multiple perspectives.
teachers' ERB is a complex and multidimensional construct.
